newsitem.title: GERMANY: Pace of German intervention grain offers slowing.
newsitem.headline: Pace of German intervention grain offers slowing.

text.p: Some 10,468 tonnes of feed rye and 20,940 tonnes of barley have been offered to German intervention board BLE over the last week, a BLE source said on Monday.
Last week, rye offers totalled 33,472 tonnes and barley offers 23,973 tonnes.
Traders said offers should slow in May, the last month in the November-May intervention campaign.
They did not expect much more wheat to arrive because of high prices in the free market.
Total 1996/97 campagin offers lag those in the same 95/96 period.
Total grain volumes offered by April 25 totalled 1,050,423 tonnes compared with 1,662,738 tonnes a year earlier.
The offers are volumes that were accepted, but have not yet been delivered to stores, by the close last Friday.
Sellers may withdraw offers and BLE may refuse acceptance on quality grounds.
The May buying-in price for all grains will be 247.98 marks/tonne.
